title: Hybrid Commitment Pricing for High-throughput Rerank: SLA-weighted Per-Vector Experiment
creator: Maya Alvarez
description:
Background: A set of enterprise customers with reranking-heavy workloads have requested lower per-vector unit costs but require strict latency SLAs and predictable monthly spend. Pure per-vector discounts (volume slabs) favor batch-oriented customers and can degrade economics for low-latency rerankers.

Objective: Design and pilot a hybrid pricing experiment that blends a capped per-vector unit price with an SLA-weighted commitment credit. The goal is to align economics with customer value (latency-sensitive rerank requests) while preserving unit economics for Redwood and supporting enterprise contract flows and QSA requirements.

Hypothesis: Introducing an SLA-weighted commitment (monthly committed spend + latency-tier credits) will convert 20% of targeted pilot customers from month-to-month usage to 6–12 month commitments while maintaining >= 10% margin uplift vs. baseline volume-discount slabs.

Experiment design:
- Offer: two commitment tiers (Committed Bronze / Silver) that combine a per-vector unit at ~10% below list and a monthly SLA credit redeemable against overage charges if latency SLOs are met.
- Measurement windows: 30d baseline, 90d pilot.
- Eligibility: customers with median rerank latency <= 60ms p95 and monthly vector volume > 10M.
- Billing model: committed monthly spend converted to credits; overages billed at committed per-vector rate; failure to meet SLA reduces credit and can trigger automatic rollback to standard rates.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Commercial: conversion to commitment >= 20% of invited cohort; average committed ARR >= $25k/customer.
- Economic: effective unit cost to Redwood >= target margin (target margin = baseline margin + 10%).
- Reliability: <2 incidents where SLA enforcement disagrees with telemetry in a 90d period.
- Product: telemetry hooks implemented (per-route latency tagging for credits) and Console reporting for customers.

Implementation notes:
- Require runtime telemetry changes to annotate vectors with rerank-label and latency buckets. Engineering work scoped under ENG-48612 (instrumentation) and ENG-48655 (billing pipeline delta).
- QSA/security: provide a targeted QSA packet showing data flow (no PII in vectors), encryption-at-rest and in-transit, and an audit trail for credits/rollbacks. Security questionnaire template updated and linked.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: SLA enforcement edge cases may credit customers incorrectly -> mitigation: conservative rollout with manual verification for first 5 customers.
- Risk: cannibalization of existing slab-based enterprise deals -> mitigation: limit pilot to new commitments and require sales approval for migrations.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal pilot with 3 strategic accounts (30d). 2) Expand to 10 accounts (90d) if telemetry and margin targets met. 3) Productize pricing slab and console UI for credits in pricing-2026-q2 release.
